description: Selected exact native EventBridge bus-target controls and delivery evidence. SDK replay uses local root credentials for each captured account; IAM execution roles and resource policies are real. Request IDs, SQS receipts and observer polling omitted. Actual event bytes and semantic envelopes remain separate; replay normalizes only generated IDs/time.
scope: Six disjoint native graphs now exercise mixed account/region forwarding: A east to B east to B west or C west delivers; A east to B west to local B west or C west delivers; A east to B west to B east or original-account A east fails with THIRD_REGION_HOP_DETECTED. Each graph has exact intermediary direct-ingress positive controls, per-edge NO_PERMISSIONS DLQ controls, and two final submissions with identical outcomes. Same-region forwarding preserves the complete incoming envelope; cross-region forwarding changes id/time but retains the ORIGINAL account/region.

Missing same-region, cross-region and admitted-then-deleted destinations now have a 665.978-second native observation with exact positive and denied-role controls, source witnesses and published invocation counters. The evidence supports acknowledged/drop behavior but does not invent destination data, measured zero counters, NO_RESOURCE, or a future terminal outcome; see missing_destination_evidence.

Actual delivery timestamps are SQS Attributes.SentTimestamp; observations additionally record RFC3339 observed_at. Poll-window absence is not proof that no later delivery was possible. Original corpus windows retain exact bounds and all subsequent queues were drained until teardown.

The cross-account PutTargets API documentation describes role retention when omitted; current native service instead rejected omission while preserving the record. Historical/pre-March-2023 targets were not tested.

[INFERENCE] Cross-region and same-region forwarding consume independent history allowances, regardless of whether account changes concurrently. AWS internal counters/metadata were not inspected; this is a model consistent with observed graph behavior, not an observed implementation.

runs.scope: Five disjoint rules created by account B on account A’s bus. Each caller supplies its own-account target role. aws:SourceArn names the rule in A; aws:SourceAccount is A, not the creator or role account. Setup settled for 20 seconds before publication. The earlier shared-target update experiment is not used as a trust-context oracle.

missing_destination_evidence.interpretation: Bounded native observations, not emulator metric coverage. Three rounds supplied nine events per rule. The real-bus control delivered nine and the denied-role control dead-lettered nine; all 45 originating IDs reached the source witness. Missing buses produced no observed DLQ outcome. Missing samples are absent, not measured zeros. The denied-role control also has SuccessfulInvocationAttempts, so this counter alone does not prove forwarding delivery or universal terminal behavior.
